mutants.reason: Memory would store on non-accepted cycles and skip accepted writes, so words are lost or corrupted.
The write FSM could leave REL while the acknowledge is still 1, because the read pointer is already 0. o_sw_rst_busy would then fall early.
The read block would be inverted. o_empty would be 1 in normal running and 0 during a software reset.
A software reset would start only if the low level and a pending request were both present, so a plain i_rst_n_sw low pulse would no longer start a sequence.
o_overflow would be 1 during hardware reset instead of 0.
The read FSM could leave ACK before the write pointer is seen as 0 or the request has dropped, which breaks the flush handshake and the reset timing.
The registered empty flag would be inverted, so o_empty would be wrong in every state.
The read pointer would advance when no read is accepted and hold when one is, so the read order and occupancy would be wrong.
o_empty_thr would reset to 0 instead of 1.
o_underflow would be 1 during hardware reset instead of 0.
o_sw_rst_busy would be inverted: 1 when idle and 0 during a sequence.
The request to the read side would be inverted, so the read side would be blocked in idle and the handshake would break.
The write pointer would advance on non-accepted cycles and hold on accepted writes, so occupancy and full would be wrong.
o_full_thr would reset to 1 instead of 0. With no block it would show 1 after hardware reset until the first edge.
The read pointer would wrap at the wrong value, which breaks the modulo-2xDEPTH counting.
The read pointer would be cleared in every state except RST, so normal reads would not advance it and it would not be cleared by the software reset.
The registered empty flag would reset to 0, so o_empty would be 0 after hardware reset on an empty FIFO.
The acknowledge would reset to 1. After a hardware reset in the middle of a sequence the write side would see a stale ack and its busy timing would change.
The write pointer would wrap at the wrong value, which breaks the modulo-2xDEPTH counting and the full flag.
The REL exit condition would be inverted, so the sequence would stay in REL or leave it at the wrong time. o_sw_rst_busy timing would change or it would never fall.
o_full would reset to 1 instead of 0.
The ACK exit would require a non-zero write pointer, so the read FSM would stay in ACK and reads would stay blocked.
The read FSM would leave RUN when there is no request and would not react to a request, so the software reset would not clear the read pointer.
The request would be 1 when the next state is not HOLD and 0 in HOLD, so the request handshake and the read-side block timing would change.
The HOLD exit would be inverted, so the sequence would leave HOLD while i_rst_n_sw is low and would stay in HOLD after it returns to 1.
o_sw_rst_busy would reset to 1 instead of 0.
The acknowledge would be inverted, so the write FSM would see a wrong handshake and the sequence would stall or run at the wrong time.
The ACK exit condition would be inverted, so the read FSM would leave ACK at the wrong time or stay there.
The request would be 1 in every state except PTR, which breaks the handshake and the read-side blocking.
The REQ exit would be inverted, so the write FSM would leave REQ without the acknowledge and would stall when it arrives. The pointer clear and the busy timing would change.
The delayed request would reset to 1, so a falling edge of i_rst_n_sw right after hardware reset would not be seen as a new request in REQ or PTR.
The read pointer would be cleared in every state except RST, so normal reads would not advance it and the pointer would not be cleared by the software reset.
The read-domain reset branch would be inverted, so normal operation would hold the reset values and hardware reset would not clear the state.

The write-domain reset branch would be inverted, so normal operation would hold the reset values and hardware reset would not clear the state.
The pending request flag would reset to 1. After hardware reset the FSM would start a spurious software reset sequence, so o_sw_rst_busy and o_full would go high.
